 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- from respondents on account of death of Deepak S.V., son of petitioner No.1 and brother of petitioner No.2 and 3, in Road Traffic Accident.

2. In brief, petition averments are; that on 09-06- 2019 Chethan Kumar, Shivakumar and his mother have visited a temple at Channgiri Taluk near Santhebennur in vehicle, bearing No.KA-18-N-6417, they have left the temple on 10-06-2019 early morning at 4.30 a.m., when they reached near Imangala, Hiriyur Taluk, in between Ganesh Temple and Poultry Farm, they noticed that one Pulsar vehicle was passing in front of them had suddenly taken a turn and in order to avoid an accident, he had 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 taken a turn and hit a stone, as a result of which Chethan Kumar had suffered injuries to his right leg and Shivakumar had suffered injuries to his left leg and Shivakumar's mother Smt. Jayamma died on the spot as she suffered severe head injury for the reason that car had fallen into the gutter beside the stone and since there was a severe injury caused to Deepak S.V. on his head, he died on the way to the hospital in the ambulance.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as Store Manager at Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd., Sira and earning a sum of Rs.23,990/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death petitioners lost the dependency, love and affection.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. Respondent No.2 remained absent and therefore he was placed exparte.

3(a). Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Skoda Fabia, bearing No.KA-18-N-6417 and its validity as on the date of accident, denied the other petition averments generally and it contended that this Tribunal has no jurisdiction to entertain the petition since the petitioners are permanent resident of Sira, Tumkur District, the alleged accident took place within limits of Imangala Police Station Chitradurga District and the owner of vehicle/respondent No.2 is resident of Chikkamagaluru District.

Further, it contended that the petition is bad for 4 (SCCH-16)
MVC 5628/2019 non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act, driver of car was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, petitioner No.2 and 3 Mrs. Lakshmidevi vs M/S. Bajaj Allianz General Ins on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88950336/
2 being married sisters were not economically depending on the deceased, therefore they are not entitled for any compensation.

sentences.text: Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that Deepak S.V., succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 10-06-2019 due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Car, bearing registration No.KA-18-N- 6417?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.

What order or Award?
5.
In proof of the petition averments, petitioner No.1 to 3 got themselves examined as PW1 to PW3 and marked documents in Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
Respondent No.1 did not lead its evidence.
Respondent No.2 is exparte. 5 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 6.
Heard counsel for petitioners and respondent No.1.

Perused the pleadings and evidences, on the basis, findings on the issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following REASONS ISSUE No.1:
7.
Petitioners led oral as well as documentary evidences.
Respondent No.1 did not lead evidence except cross examining PWs.
Respondent No.2 remained exparte.

This is a summary proceedings,
so, a sum and substance of the pleadings and evidences are only emphasized.
The petitioners need to prove this issue on preponderance of probability as test for proof is preponderance of probability herein.
The petition averments and objections of respondent No.1 are summarized herein above in the brief facts of case and objection and hence those are not repeated herein.
Respondent No.1 disputed the negligence and dependency.

The incident, involvement of vehicle, injuries and death,
insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.

8. Regarding the negligence is concerned the petitioners relied on police records viz., ture copy of FIR 6 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 with Complaint, Charge Sheet, IMV Report, Spot Mahazar and PM Report, which are marked in Ex.P1 to Ex.P5.

The charge sheet/final report filed by the Imangala Police shows the negligence by the driver of car, bearing No.KA-18-N-6417, the brief facts of the final report are extracted hereunder for better appreciation:

sentences.text: 9. The spot mahazar depicts the scene of occurrence.
The Motor Vehicle Accident Report reveals 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 that there was no mechanical defects in the vehicle, and the damages.
The postmortem report shows the cause of death was due to head injury sustained.
According to the IMV report there was no mechanical defects in the vehicle in the sense the incident was due to the negligence only.
No eyewitness is examined herein.

Here being no contrary evidence by respondent No.1 and nothing is elicited in cross-examination of PW1 regarding the version of respondent No.1 and hence here is no impediment to believe the police documents regarding the negligence.
The police documents give right impression that due to the negligence of the driver of the car the incident occurred.
Thus, the police records are considered.

10. Regarding the territorial jurisdiction of this tribunal is concerned as objected to by respondent No.1 as per the verdict of hon'ble the Apex Court the business of the insurer having scope of entire nation the petitioners being at liberty to opt to file the present petition is not barred by the territorial jurisdiction for adjudication.
11.

Regarding objections by respondent No.1 as to non compliance of provision under Section 134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act is concerned as the petition reached its finality and the petitioners approached the Tribunal, respondent No.1 had already taken all the contentions 8 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 of respondent No.2 the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act, and discussion on the same now does not arise.
12. Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that Deepak S.V., succumbed to the injuries met with motor vehicle accident on 10-06-2019 and died due to the rash and negligent driving of driver car bearing No.KA-18-N- 6417.
Hence, this issue is answered affirmatively.

ISSUE No.2:
13.
In determination of this issue avocation, income, age of the deceased, dependency and future prospects and other conventional heads for compensation are need to be ascertained.

sentences.text: 4 Avocation :
It is averred that the deceased was working as Store Manager at Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd., Sira and earning a sum of Rs.23,990/- per month.
In substantiation of the same the petitioners have produced pay slip for the month of May, June and July 2019 and bank statement as per Ex.P11 and Ex.P12.
But, they have not examined the author of Ex.P11.
Therefore, they are not considered.
Hence, no other option but to consider notional income of the deceased in the present case.
As per Ex.P8 - SSLC marks card, date of birth of deceased was 19-01-1986 and so that age of the deceased was 33 years at the time of incident.
Hence, they are considered.
Income:
As discussed on the head of avocation, the deceased's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2019 came to be fixed at 14,000/.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.14,000/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the deceased per month.
Dependency:
As per the petition averments petitioner No.1 is mother and petitioner No.2 and 3 are sisters of deceased.
The monetary dependency is disputed by respondent No.1.
Petitioner No.2 who is sister of the deceased admitted in her cross-examination that she was not monetarily depended on the deceased.
Thus, monetary dependency of petitioner No.1 and 3 are not in dispute.
Ex. P6, Ex.P9 and Ex.P10 - aadhar cards prove the identification of petitioners.

Whereas, for deduction of personal expenses is concerned, the deceased was a bachelor, 50% is considered to be deducted in the monthly notional income for the personal and living expenses of deceased.
Future prospects:

The future prospects is concerned, the age of deceased at the time of the death was 33 years, so as per the principle laid down in Hem Raj vs. The Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd., and others case, reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (SC), 40% needs to be added to the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: So, 40% is added to the monthly notional income of deceased.
Thus, 40% of addition will come to Rs.5,600/-.
In total, the monthly notional income will be Rs.19,600/-.

sentences.text: Conventional Heads:
Consortium:
The deceased being son of petitioner No.1 and brother of petitioner No.2 and 3 filial consortium are to be considered as the petitioners suffered the loss of love and affection.

Hence, in view of observations made, in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others, in civil Appeal No.2705/2020, by hon'ble Apex Court, Rs.40,000/- each is considered to be awarded as compensation for consortium respectively.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 Loss of estate:

The loss of estate is concerned, as the deceased was with the family, if the incident could not have been occurred, he could have been contributed more or less from his savings to the estate of family; the incident caused such loss to the estate of petitioners.
Hence, Rs.15,000/- is need to be awarded on this head as the principle laid down by hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Funeral Expenses:
As per the observation made by hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi case for the funeral expenses is concerned awarding of Rs.15,000/- is also just under the conventional head.
Hence, it is awarded.
14. Accordingly, compensation is calculated as under;
Monthly notional income of Rs.14,000/-.
Future prospects in 40% on the monthly notional income is Rs.5,600/-.
Monthly notional income + future prospects = 19,600/-.

For personal and living expenses, after the deduction of 50%, the total monthly notional income is Rs.9,800/-.
12 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 Net monthly notional income is Rs.9,800/- is calculated to net annual income as Rs.9,800/- x 12 which is = 1,17,600/-.
Multiplier is 16.
Net annual income is multiplied by multiplier 16, which is as Rs.1,17,600/- x 16, will come to Rs.18,81,600/-.

sentences.text: So, compensation for loss of dependency is found at Rs.18,81,600/- plus compensation on conventional heads, such as filial consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

16. The details of compensation proposed to be awarded are as under:
 Sl. Head of  Amount/Rs  No. Compensation  1. Loss of dependency 18,81,600-00  2. Loss of filial consortium 1,20,000-00
3 . Loss of estate 15,000-00
4. Funeral expenses 15,000-00  Total 20,31,600-00 17.
In all, petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,31,600/-.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 considered to be directed till its realization.
So, the petitioners are entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.

Liability:
18. Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the offending car.
On vicarious liability respondent No.2 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.1 being the insurer of respondent No.2 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.1 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioners are only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
19.
In view of the findings on issue No.1 and 2, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.20,31,600/- (Rupees 14 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 twenty lakhs, thirty one thousand and six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Compensation amount is  apportioned as follows:-
 Petitioner No.1 - Mother 50%

 Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.1 to 3

, 25% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released to them through E- 15 (SCCH-16) MVC 5628/2019 payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
